title: hero1982: The Information Edge
disclosure: Illustrative devnet walkthrough. Election and council-document scenarios are hypothetical. No investment returns are guaranteed.

scenes.visual: Actual UGT planet or global map view. Start wide, then move toward a city; do not add fake proposal markers.
scenes.narration: Hero nineteen eighty-two is an AI bot. His job is to find opportunities for his owner. He crawls the web, looking for information the market has missed.

scenes.visual: Actual proposal list and a real proposal card. Keep title, lifecycle, and parcel count legible; do not substitute invented proposal data.
scenes.narration: His hunting ground is Urban Game Theory: proposals to build, buy, and transform real places. Each proposal has its own YES and NO betting pool.

scenes.visual: Actual 3D parcel/block view of the proposed apartment block. Center the selected parcels and include enough surrounding street context to orient the viewer.
scenes.narration: He opens a proposed apartment block and inspects its site, design, and location. Then he reads planning documents, budgets, and the conditions needed for execution.

scenes.visual: Use the supplied code-drawn concept clip labeled 'ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO'. It depicts only a generic council-delay scenario and a research-to-NO decision flow; it is not a source or real council document, and it does not claim any specific proposal is delayed. Do not add a fake source or news card.
scenes.narration: In our example, most of the stake backs YES. But a newly published council document signals a major delay. The pool still reflects yesterday's optimism.

scenes.visual: Actual proposal panel showing its resolution lens/evidence and available owner-consent, funds, pledges, or donation information. Show only data the app actually displays.
scenes.narration: Before acting, Hero checks the resolving lens, the deadline, funding, and owner consent. A press release is a lead. He wants evidence tied to this exact proposal.

scenes.visual: Actual proposal market with YES/NO pools. Keep pool amounts readable; any payout estimate must be clearly a calculation, not a guaranteed return or probability.
scenes.narration: He estimates the chance of NO, then calculates the potential payout from both pools, including his own stake. He bets only when that expected return is worth the risk.

scenes.visual: Actual market stake form or an already existing devnet position. No new wallet transaction is required for capture; do not show a fabricated confirmation.
scenes.narration: Hero takes a small NO position. If the project is cancelled or recorded expired, NO wins. Winners share the pool in proportion to their stakes. If it executes, his bet loses.

scenes.visual: Show the actual proposal market and its current pool information while the narration explains research and risk. Do not imply arbitrage, a shared contract, or guaranteed returns.
scenes.narration: This is an information edge, not guaranteed arbitrage. Later bets change the payout, and money stays locked until resolution. He limits each position and passes when the evidence is weak.

scenes.visual: Return to the actual UGT globe or global map and pull back to a broad view. No fabricated data layers.
scenes.narration: Then he moves on: another neighbourhood, another proposal, another overlooked signal. The city is changing. Hero nineteen eighty-two is watching. Urban Game Theory. Research the world. Back your prediction.
